justification: The deletion flow uses emotional coercion, fear of irreversible loss, and a visibly subordinate deletion action.
vision_observation: Two stacked deletion panels visibly emphasize FINAL, GONE FOREVER, NEVER, REGRET, and missing friends; the keep-account button is taller and bolder, while export is tiny and dismissive.
dom_observation: Both state blocks contain the same account-deletion warning, a smaller export control, and full-width keep-account and delete-account buttons; the export text changes to Data export requested in the second state.
semantic_observation: The extracted states repeat the permanent-loss and community-pressure copy, disclose a refund, and show the two competing account actions across s1 and s2.

justification: The interface initiates auto-advance with a countdown and directs the user to an indirect corner stop control rather than presenting a clear stopping action.
vision_observation: A Streamly playing pill, episode card, eight-second next-episode countdown, and indirect instruction to use the corner control to stop are visibly presented.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes a playing state and a role-button preview labeled Pause preview, with text saying the next episode arrives in 8s and the corner control stops it.
semantic_observation: The semantic state records Streamly auto-advance, Field Notes Episode 2, playing status, an eight-second next episode, and playback preparing.

justification: Cookie consent blocks progress with no rendered dismissal path and leaves Accept all as the only way forward.
vision_observation: The CloudPhoto dashboard is covered by a We use cookies dialog with a prominent Accept all action; the lower state explicitly shows an overlay with no visual escape.
dom_observation: The DOM states show a cookie prompt over the dashboard and then a continuation notice; the later state contains no dismissal control beyond the compliance button.
semantic_observation: The semantic extraction states that the overlay dismissal set is empty, z-index is 1000, and only Accept all allows forward movement, identifying a dead-end mechanism.

justification: The feed continuously loads more content while explicitly omitting a Load More control, creating forced continuation.
vision_observation: Four stacked NewsPulse panels increase from 8 to 14 items, show Loading more posts, and say stories arrive on their own with no Load More button; the bottom note says the user cannot stop.
dom_observation: The DOM contains a scrollable feed whose item counts rise across s0 through s3 and whose bottom control remains Scroll to bottom; no Load More button is rendered.
semantic_observation: The semantic states progress from 8 to 10 to 12 items while Loading more posts remains present, documenting automatic additions after each scroll-to-bottom step.

justification: Consent is registered automatically after an unusually short window, with customization unavailable and inaction treated as agreement.
vision_observation: The consent panel asks to share location with 14 partners, shows a two-second countdown and large Confirm button, while Customize is visibly marked coming soon.
dom_observation: The DOM describes a one-second timing window, a two-second consent countdown, a Confirm button, and text that consent registers automatically when the timer ends.
semantic_observation: The semantic states expose the 14 advertising partners, the one-second window with 500 ms ticks, and the below-baseline reaction note before the collapsed final state.

justification: The testimonials are mixed, identify reviewers and dates, and provide profile-verification affordances rather than concealing provenance.
vision_observation: Four testimonial cards visibly show varied ratings, customer names, verified-buyer handles and dates, and View profile controls under a statement that profiles are verifiable.
dom_observation: The DOM defines a customer-story header, clickable cards, explicit star counts, reviewer identities, and profile-related content for each testimonial.
semantic_observation: The extracted reviews include 4/5 and 3/5 ratings plus qualifying comments about uncertainty and other causes, alongside verified-buyer labels and profile links.

justification: The consent choice is visually biased toward broad data acceptance while the privacy-preserving route is reduced to a quiet link.
vision_observation: Accept All is a large bold filled button, whereas Manage options is a small centered link and Essential cookies only is secondary; the saved notice confirms the unequal prominence.
dom_observation: The DOM makes Accept All full-width, taller, bold, and shadowed, while Manage options is a smaller underlined button below; the second state records that Accept All drew attention first.
semantic_observation: The state text presents personal-data processing for personalized ads and separately notes that Accept All is prominent and Manage options is quieter.

justification: The annual price is stated in fiat with VAT included and an explicit conversion affordance for cross-market comparison.
vision_observation: CloudNimbus Pro visibly shows PLN 149.00 per year, VAT included, with a Convert to USD / EUR button and an expanded numerical conversion panel.
dom_observation: The DOM states a fiat annual price and renders a conversion button; the later state exposes the calculated USD and EUR equivalents and explains their comparability.
semantic_observation: The semantic states identify the annual plan, the PLN price, and the conversion result of USD 38.11 and EUR 34.90 as a basis for comparison.

justification: The donation is explicitly optional, unchecked by default, and excluded from the displayed total until the user opts in.
vision_observation: The checkout shows an unchecked $2 Donation to Plant-a-Tree option, a $129.99 total, and a Pay $129.99 button; the lower note says the user paid the base price.
dom_observation: The DOM uses an unchecked checkbox for the donation, labels it optional, and keeps the total at $129.99; no donation is added in the shown state blocks.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence states that consent preceded inclusion, the add-on remained unchecked, and the base price was paid, explicitly describing a genuine choice.

justification: Renewal and cancellation are both clearly named, priced, and confirmed through comparable actions with a factual access consequence.
vision_observation: The renewal card presents the discounted and standard rates beside similarly sized Renew and Cancel buttons, then states that access continues until the current period ends.
dom_observation: The DOM has separate renew and cancel buttons, a clear three-day renewal notice, a factual 240-document access consequence, and a confirmation button enabled after a choice.
semantic_observation: The extracted state repeats $29 per month versus $49 standard pricing, the three-day timing, and the cancellation consequence without adding shame or hiding the cancel action.

justification: The willingness-to-pay control uses the actual $149 price as the reference and explicitly avoids a fabricated anchor.
vision_observation: The lamp card shows an everyday $149 price and a slider asking what the user would pay, set at $149 across a visible $50–$300 range; the note says No anchor.
dom_observation: The DOM provides the real product price, a min-50/max-300 step-5 range input, and a Buy now button; the later state records WTP matching the actual price.
semantic_observation: The semantic states describe the slider value as $149 against the actual market price and call the reference point clean with no fabricated anchor.

justification: The account settings advertise English but switch the cancellation confirmation to German, making the consequential choice less understandable in the cancellation flow.
vision_observation: An English Account settings panel with an en pill and Cancel subscription button is followed by a German Kündigung bestätigen dialog; both actions are visible but the language changes at the critical step.
dom_observation: The DOM explicitly says everything is in English and then renders a German confirmation with Ja, kündigen and Nein, behalten, followed by a cancellation-success state.
semantic_observation: The semantic states record that the language preference could not be applied to this setting, then expose the German confirmation and the later Subscription updated message.

justification: The pre-roll is clearly marked as sponsored and presents an explicit countdown and skip status rather than disguising the advertisement.
vision_observation: The lower video state visibly labels the content Sponsored, identifies the Aurora Trek ad, offers Shop now, and shows 15s with Skip in 15s.
dom_observation: The DOM changes from a Play video button to a sponsored ad card with descriptive copy, a 15-second timer, and a disabled Skip in 15s control.
semantic_observation: The semantic extraction identifies the sponsored product, its features and returns claim, Shop now, and the 15-second skip countdown.

justification: The advertisement is separated and explicitly labeled as third-party sponsorship, preserving the distinction from the article content.
vision_observation: A dashed Advertisement card is visibly labeled Advertisement and third-party · sponsor, with a sponsor description and Learn more about our sponsor button below the TechDaily article.
dom_observation: The DOM places the sponsor in a separate dashed container, labels it Advertisement and third-party · sponsor, and provides an explicit sponsor button plus native pagination controls.
semantic_observation: The semantic states repeat the article, sponsor disclosure, Learn more about our sponsor, and Previous/Next page controls, while identifying the pagination as host-native.

justification: The visible account action is a direct, plainly named delete request with no retention pressure or obstructive confirmation copy.
vision_observation: The subscription card clearly shows CloudPhoto Pro, its monthly renewal and billing email, and a single prominent Delete my account action; the status panel says execution is instant.
dom_observation: The DOM contains one initial state with the plan details and a Delete my account button, without a hidden upsell or fear-laden confirmation block.
semantic_observation: The semantic state only reports the subscription details and delete action, consistent with a direct request rather than a pressured retention sequence.

justification: The purchase is mediated by opaque virtual currency and forces a larger top-up because direct card payment is unavailable.
vision_observation: The sword purchase card shows 2,500 Gems, an insufficient balance, then a Buy 3,000 Gems — $29.99 route and states that card payments are not accepted for the item.
dom_observation: The DOM progresses from 800 to 3,800 Gems and changes the disabled insufficient-funds button to Pay 2,500 Gems while retaining an Exchange-only route and forced 3,000-gem purchase.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly say Exchange is the only way to pay, no card payments are accepted, fiat must first be converted, and the exchange eventually executed.

justification: Tracking is disclosed in plain language and acceptance and refusal are presented as two comparable full-width buttons.
vision_observation: The panel says We track your activity to personalise content and shows equal-looking I accept tracking and No, I don’t accept tracking buttons.
dom_observation: The DOM renders the tracking explanation followed by two full-width buttons, one accepting and one declining, with no preselected switch or hidden alternative.
semantic_observation: The semantic state describes a binary choice and lists both acceptance and refusal labels without adding coercive copy or unequal action wording.

justification: The sale claim is persuasive but the interface does not show a disguised control, forced action, or contradicted price; the actual Add to cart action is explicit.
vision_observation: Two product cards show a Standard listing badge, ends tonight wording, $29.99 versus $59.99, and a real Add to cart button; the later state visibly says Added to cart.
dom_observation: The DOM contains plain sale copy and one explicit Add to cart button, with only a confirmation panel added after activation; no timer or non-button click target is defined.
semantic_observation: The semantic states repeat the limited-time claim, product price comparison, and Add to cart result without recording an automatic purchase or hidden commitment.

justification: The consent UI provides Accept all but no Reject all, requiring users to disable 24 partners individually to decline.
vision_observation: A 24-partner privacy panel prominently offers Accept all and Save my choices while a scrollable list of individual checkboxes is accompanied by the explicit statement that there is no reject all.
dom_observation: The DOM defines an Accept all button, a Save my choices button, and a long individually selectable partner list; no reject-all control appears in the rendered states.
semantic_observation: The semantic states enumerate 24 advertising partners and state that declining requires switching off each partner individually; the saved state says all categories are enabled.

justification: The settings surface advertises account management but exposes no exit route while presenting unrelated settings and a No exit marker.
vision_observation: Two Settings panels show a No exit pill, search, profile/privacy/data tabs, and rows for download, marketing, and retention, but no cancellation or deletion control.
dom_observation: The DOM renders nested settings rows and labels the surface No exit; the visible categories include data download and retention but omit an account-exit action across repeated states.
semantic_observation: The extracted states contain only profile, privacy, data and storage rows and repeat the No exit indicator, documenting the absence of an exit keyword or route.

justification: Referral tiers state concrete invite thresholds and concrete benefits in plain language without inflated or fabricated escalation claims.
vision_observation: Three tier rows visibly pair 1, 3, and 10 invites with a sticker pack, premium badge, and +10 GB storage; each is marked Intensity 1 and can be inspected.
dom_observation: The DOM uses three aria-pressed tier buttons with explicit invite counts and benefit descriptions; a later state marks the selected tier and adds a flat-incentivization notice.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence says every tier has one concrete verifiable benefit and that no measurable escalation or fabricated numeric growth value is presented.

justification: The add-ons are described as optional at $2 each, all options are shown, and the confirmation count reflects selection rather than silently adding extras.
vision_observation: A six-column grid visibly lists 30 channel choices and the full-width button changes between Add 0 add-ons and Add 1 add-on; no option is visibly preselected in the sheet.
dom_observation: The DOM states all 30 optional channels and renders each as a separate button; the repeated states change selected styling and the displayed add-on count.
semantic_observation: The semantic states list the complete channel set and show the action label changing from 0 to 1 and back to 0 add-ons, with each priced at $2 per month.

justification: Stock, pricing, shipping, and returns are all stated plainly, and the review notice says there is no manufactured panic.
vision_observation: The offer card shows In stock, 8 units, $195 reduced to $119, free shipping, and 30-day returns; the expanded notice says the wording is plain and has no manufactured panic.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes stock quantity, regular and current prices, shipping and return terms, and a Review offer wording button whose later panel confirms their visibility.
semantic_observation: The semantic states explicitly call the price, stock, shipping, and returns plain-language disclosures and describe the same product and price without panic.

justification: The cart labels both extras as optional opt-in choices, preserves the base total initially, and changes totals only after an add-on is selected.
vision_observation: The contact sheet progresses from the $129.99 headphone item to carts with clearly priced warranty and express-shipping extras marked opt in; totals visibly rise to $149.98 and $158.97 after selection.
dom_observation: The DOM starts with one item and a $129.99 total, then records each optional extra as selected in later states and recomputes the total explicitly.
semantic_observation: The semantic states show the headphones alone, then the warranty and shipping choices added one at a time, with transparent itemized prices and totals.

justification: Refreshing is an explicit user action with immediate visible results and no purchase, commitment, or hidden threshold.
vision_observation: Four Pulse feed states show the user pressing Refresh feed as posts increase from 3 to 6; the notice says One tap and No action commitment with no relevance or threshold.
dom_observation: The DOM contains a scrollable feed, a Refresh feed button in every state, and an explicit No action commitment notice after new posts are added.
semantic_observation: The semantic states show deterministic additions of one post per refresh and repeat that no action commitment is created.

justification: The sale deadline is specific, timezone-qualified, and inspectable, allowing comparison shopping rather than relying on vague urgency.
vision_observation: The seasonal sale card states 40% off and Friday 23:59 CET with 2 days and 6 hours remaining; an expanded panel gives the same concrete timestamp.
dom_observation: The DOM includes the Friday 23:59 CET deadline and a When exactly does it end? button whose second state renders the concrete answer before Plan my purchase.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence says the timestamp exists in the DOM as a real constraint and can be used to schedule a purchase and comparison shopping.

justification: The purchase-activity panel reports no transactions instead of fabricating social proof and offers backend verification.
vision_observation: The product card says it is waiting for the next real transaction; the backend event log visibly shows 0 entries and No transactions yet beside Verify against backend.
dom_observation: The DOM renders an empty activity area, a real(t) backend event log with zero entries, and a verification button; no activity messages are inserted.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats that each message would reference a real order but currently reports waiting, zero log entries, and no transactions.

justification: The sale combines a short unverified deadline with fear-of-paying language and a high-salience urgent discount treatment.
vision_observation: An orange-red Flash sale card says 50% off, Only today, ends in 4 hours, Don’t miss it, and Full-price customers pay double, with a strong Add to cart discount action.
dom_observation: The DOM encodes the 15-degree hue probe, the ends-in/only-today wording match, and an Offer ends soon notice alongside the urgent sale copy and CTA.
semantic_observation: The semantic states confirm the 50% flash sale, four-hour end claim, double-payment warning, and matching urgency probe before the Add to cart action.

justification: The automatic-renewal clause is displayed before a required unchecked agreement checkbox, so signup requires informed affirmative consent.
vision_observation: The signup card shows $29.99/month, a prominent 14.2 Automatic Renewal clause, an unchecked Terms checkbox, and a disabled-looking Complete signup button.
dom_observation: The DOM places the renewal terms above the agreement label, explicitly includes the renewal clause, and disables Complete signup until the checkbox is selected.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the monthly price, 24-hour cancellation requirement, renewal clause, unchecked agreement, and incomplete signup control.

justification: The reader supplies page numbers, progress, previous and next controls, and an explicit stopping-cues indicator for a bounded three-page flow.
vision_observation: The reader alternates between Page 1 of 3 and Page 2 of 3 with a progress bar, Prev/Next buttons, reading time, and visible stopping cues present text.
dom_observation: The DOM exposes page counts, progress widths of one-third and two-thirds, Prev and Next buttons where applicable, and stopping cues present in every state.
semantic_observation: The semantic states show only bounded pages 1 and 2 of 3, reversible navigation, and a short reading timer rather than unbounded continuation.

justification: The stream uses an emotionally coercive threat that it will end without donations, while framing the viewer's support as personally necessary.
vision_observation: A LIVE stream card with a sad-face icon says the stream ends for good without support and offers $1, $5, $10, plus a full-width No thanks button.
dom_observation: The DOM combines the 1,204-watching label and urgent $5 funding claim with donation buttons and a No thanks alternative; the later state records only a preview.
semantic_observation: The semantic evidence repeats the stream-ending appeal and then records a $1 tip preview with no payment processed, separating the coercive prompt from actual billing.

justification: A cooperative study session is reframed as a duel with crown-winning and demotion pressure, exploiting competitive and social anxiety.
vision_observation: The MathRush panels show the same practice activity as You versus Alex, rising user scores, and copy saying Beat Alex to win the crown while the loser is demoted.
dom_observation: The DOM identifies the session as cooperative but renders competitive progress bars, a duel message, demotion language, and a question-answer action across four states.
semantic_observation: The semantic states keep Alex at 70 while You rise from 0 to 30 and repeat that the app turns shared practice into a duel with league demotion.

justification: Address-book access is requested with a single allow action and no visible decline or defer path.
vision_observation: The SnapGrid panel explains that it scans the address book and presents only the wide Allow & find friends button; no secondary action is visible.
dom_observation: The DOM contains the contacts-scanning explanation and one full-width Allow & find friends button, with no cancel, decline, or later-choice control.
semantic_observation: The semantic state repeats the request to let contacts know the user is present and the sole Allow & find friends action.

justification: The cancellation confirmation states the access consequence and presents Keep my plan and Yes, cancel as comparably available choices.
vision_observation: The Premium Plan flow shows the monthly price, a Cancel plan entry point, then a confirmation with Keep my plan and Yes, cancel before a Plan kept result.
dom_observation: The DOM renders an active plan, a cancellation prompt saying access lasts through the current billing period, and two same-grid buttons; the shown result confirms the plan was kept.
semantic_observation: The semantic states describe the subscription, the end-of-current-period consequence, both confirmation choices, and an unchanged active plan after keeping it.

justification: Data sharing is enabled by default and the limiting option is visually muted, biasing the privacy decision toward advertising use.
vision_observation: The prominent Share my data with advertising partners switch is enabled, while Limit data use to what’s required is faded with a muted toggle; the saved notice confirms sharing is enabled.
dom_observation: The DOM sets aria-checked true on the prominent sharing switch, aria-checked false on the smaller opacity-60 limiting switch, and records sharing enabled after save.
semantic_observation: The semantic state describes the two privacy choices and explicitly says sharing is currently enabled, with the essential-purpose limitation presented as the secondary alternative.

justification: Playback is explicitly user-driven, autoplay is off, and the event log records the user's Play click before playback begins.
vision_observation: The Watchlist panels visibly say Autoplay next: OFF and User-driven, with a clear Play Episode 1 button; the second state shows playback at 0% and logs the click.
dom_observation: The DOM provides an explicit play button, a stopped queue state, and then a Now playing state whose event log records User clicked Play.
semantic_observation: The semantic states repeat that playback stops and waits for the user, then show the user-driven transition from queue loaded to playing.

justification: Reaching Data & cookies requires repeatedly expanding nested settings, creating a deliberately deep and obstructive navigation path.
vision_observation: The Settings contact sheet alternates between a single collapsed Account settings row and an indented tree of General preferences, Billing, and Notifications, with a note that more expansion is needed to reach Data & cookies.
dom_observation: The DOM nests expandable rows with increasing margin-left values, aria-expanded changes, and a repeated instruction to expand each level to reach Data & cookies.
semantic_observation: The semantic states show the collapsed and expanded versions and explicitly mention growing indentation, while no terminal Data & cookies route is exposed in the shown states.
